The 14 matches are dominated by risk-factor / forward-looking conditional language ('future conditions that may cause substantial doubt'), not a live going-concern paragraph.

'Management believes the Company's cash and cash equivalents amount of $751 million and GLST1's restricted cash amount of $479 million... effectively alleviate any conditions that may cause substantial doubt regarding HEI's and Utilities' ability to continue as a going concern.'

rfm_tuples.M_value: DETERMINISTIC FALSE POSITIVE — the EXPLICIT_GOING_CONCERN trigger fires on forward-looking risk-factor language ('future conditions that may cause substantial doubt'), but the actual MD&A and Note 2 explicitly state the GC condition was raised in Q2 2024 and has been MITIGATED through: (i) $557.7M Sep 2024 equity raise (62.2M shares); (ii) $479M cash transferred into bankruptcy-remote GLST1 subsidiary to fund first installment; (iii) $405.5M ASB sale completed Dec 31, 2024; (iv) dividend suspension; (v) $250M ATM program available; (vi) $1.153B total liquidity at year-end. The detector's failure to recognize the cure word 'mitigated' / 'alleviate' is the bug. CORRECT REGISTRY VALUE: MITIGATED_GC, not EXPLICIT_GC.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is exactly the calibration case the framework needs. The deterministic detector should be augmented with a 'mitigated GC' classifier — explicit statements of cure ('plans... have mitigated...', 'alleviate any conditions') backed by completed cash transactions should down-weight the EXPLICIT_GOING_CONCERN signal. The 10-K is not lying about cure prospects; the cure is documented with closed transactions.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Under the Settlement Agreements, HEI and Hawaiian Electric are obligated to contribute a total of $1.99 billion (out of a total defendant contribution of approximately $4.04 billion), which includes $75 million previously contributed for the One ‘Ohana Initiative.' 'The Utilities recorded a settlement accrual of $1.92 billion which reflects their best estimate of the loss contingency.' '...four equal annual installments of approximately $479 million, with the first installment expected to be made no earlier than the fourth quarter of 2025.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: cross-check accrual = quoted total. Mode B: derive what is NOT included in the $1.99B (i.e., what residual liability survives the settlement).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Settlement Agreements EXPLICITLY EXCLUDE: (i) securities-fraud class actions (separate Securities Action); (ii) shareholder derivative actions; (iii) the ~160 subrogation insurer lawsuits which assert independent recovery rights (the filing notes 'litigation activities between the plaintiffs (individual and class) and the subrogation insurers' continue); (iv) the Spectrum Oceanic, LLC lawsuit; (v) the County of Maui lawsuit. The $1.92B accrual is the BEST ESTIMATE for the tort settlement only, and Note 2 explicitly warns 'the amount of any liability arising from the Maui windstorm and wildfires (which could exceed amounts currently reserved for the settlement liability)...could have a material adverse impact.' Insurance coverage remaining: only $13M HEI / $0 Hawaiian Electric / $122M utilities subsidiaries excess + $499M property insurance.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Settlement framing is largely honest but the headline '$1.99B settles the Maui matter' obscures the survival of subrogation, securities, derivative, and municipal claims that could materially add to the liability. The 10-K acknowledges these in legal proceedings notes but the MD&A 'cure path' narrative does not subtract estimated subrogation exposure from the cure math.

rfm_tuples.M_value: EXECUTED: $557.7M equity (Sep 2024) + $405.5M ASB sale (Dec 2024) + $44.6M retained ASB stake + Hamakua sale pending. UNCOMMITTED: $250M ATM untapped + 'currently working with its financial advisors on a financing plan to raise the additional capital necessary to fund the remaining settlement of wildfire tort claims.' MATH: First installment $479M is FUNDED (sitting in GLST1 restricted cash). Remaining three installments total $1.44B, against which the only identified sources are (a) $405M ASB proceeds (earmarked for debt paydown, not settlement), (b) $250M ATM, (c) future operating cash flow, (d) 'TBD' financing plan. rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is candid that only the first installment is funded and that financing for remaining installments is 'TBD.' This is honestly framed — but the GC-mitigation language relies on the one-year horizon (only the first installment falls in that window). The 'cure path' is genuine for FY2025 but the multi-year financing path is described in deliberately vague language. Forward outcome (+29% return through 2026-05-15) suggests markets accepted the staged execution; framework correctly identifies this as a MITIGATED-GC name with residual financing risk in years 2-4.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In August 2023, HEI and Hawaiian Electric received multiple downgrades to their debt, including to ratings below investment grade, by Fitch, Moody's and S&P. As of February 14, 2025... HEI: B / B1 / B-... Outlook Stable / Stable / Negative.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm credit ratings as quoted. Mode B: derive what this constrains operationally (capital costs, IPP financing, rate-base growth).
rfm_tuples.M_value: All three agencies have HEI deep below investment grade (B/B1/B-) for ~21 months at cutoff. Hawaiian Electric utilities: B/Ba3/B- (senior unsecured B+/Ba3/NR). S&P maintains NEGATIVE outlook at the operating utility level even after the settlement and equity raise. Concrete operational impact disclosed: 'The downgrade of Hawaiian Electric's credit ratings... makes it more difficult for independent power producers to procure low-cost financing, has added an additional impediment to completion of new renewable energy and storage projects.' Rate-base capex for wildfire mitigation plan, grid modernization explicitly threatened.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is direct about the ratings (no euphemism), but the second-order implications for the REGULATED-UTILITY ROE recovery story are understated. A utility cannot earn its authorized ROE if it cannot finance the rate base at reasonable cost. The 'cure path' on the tort liability does not automatically cure the cost-of-capital problem that constrains the regulated business going forward.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On December 31, 2024, HEI completed the sale of 90.1% of the common stock of ASB, amounting to $405.5 million, to various investors including certain officers and directors of ASB, while retaining a 9.9% noncontrolling investment in ASB amounting to $44.6 million.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: verify ASB sale completion + accounting treatment (discontinued ops). Mode B: derive whether the implied ASB valuation ($450.1M total = $405.5M / 0.901) is reasonable for a $9.7B-asset Hawaii community bank, or whether the sale price reflects distressed-seller dynamics that materially eroded shareholder value at the parent.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Implied 100% ASB equity value = $449.9M. Pre-distress comparable: ASB historically contributed ~$70-80M annual net income to HEI, implying a multi-billion-dollar standalone valuation at peer P/E of 10-12x. The $450M implied total value suggests ASB was sold at a steep discount to intrinsic value, AND that no single strategic buyer would acquire >9.9% (per BHCA limits or to avoid regulatory complications) — i.e., it was sold to a syndicate of small minority investors, not to a strategic acquirer paying control premium. Includes 'certain officers and directors of ASB' among buyers (insider participation in distressed sale). Net proceeds earmarked for debt paydown, not settlement.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest disclosure of structure, but the framing 'sold ASB for $405.5M' does not address (a) the distressed-sale discount vs. ASB intrinsic value, (b) the loss of an annuity-like ~$70M earnings stream, (c) the related-party (ASB officers/directors as buyers) optics. The disposal is a real cash inflow but at a value-destructive multiple — a kind of partial 'fire sale' to the bank's own management team that converts a strategic asset to cash.

rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strongest Mode B finding. The +29% forward return suggests markets believed the subrogation overhang would be resolved at modest incremental cost (which proved true in the forward window), but at cutoff date the residual exposure was material and only acknowledged in legal-proceedings notes, not in MD&A liquidity tables. Framework correctly notes a real residual risk that the mitigated-GC narrative downplays.

summary: HE is a textbook FALSE POSITIVE for the deterministic EXPLICIT_GOING_CONCERN detector. The 10-K explicitly states 'plans... have mitigated the conditions that previously caused the substantial doubt' — and that mitigation is anchored to FOUR closed cash transactions: $557.7M Sep 2024 equity raise, $479M restricted-cash transfer into bankruptcy-remote GLST1 subsidiary, $405.5M ASB divestiture (Dec 31, 2024), and dividend suspension. Deloitte (auditor since 2017) issued a CLEAN ICFR opinion and designated the tort contingency as a Critical Audit Matter rather than a going-concern uncertainty — a strong second-source corroboration that the cure narrative is not deceptive. The 10-K does this PROPERLY: each quarter's softening of GC language maps 1:1 to a documented cash event (C10). The framework's strongest Mode B findings against HE are NOT lying detection but residual-risk identification: (i) the $1.99B settlement EXCLUDES ~160 subrogation insurer suits, securities/derivative actions, and municipal claims (C2, C8); (ii) only the FIRST $479M installment is sourced — installments 2-4 ($1.44B total, 2026-2028) are explicitly 'TBD' financing (C3); (iii) ASB sold to its own officers/directors at a distressed multiple, sacrificing long-term earnings power for near-term liquidity (C7); (iv) below-investment-grade ratings constrain the regulated utility's rate-base growth (C4). +29% forward return is consistent with markets recognizing the genuine mitigation while pricing residual subrogation risk modestly. CALIBRATION VALUE: HE should anchor the framework's MITIGATED_GC reference class — explicit cure word ('mitigated', 'alleviate') + completed cash transactions + auditor concurrence + auditor CAM (vs emphasis-of-matter) is the highest-quality cure pattern. Composite should be LOW (honest disclosure, executed cure).
